# Fixture provenance

Every committed fixture that is not produced by `pdf-extract-testkit` (whose
generators are deterministic and named in `manifest.toml`) is listed here with
where it came from, its license, its SHA-256 and why it is in the corpus.
`crates/testkit/tests/fixtures_manifest.rs` checks that each such manifest
entry has a row here with the same hash.

## Generated by the test kit (corpus C)

All other files in `corpus-c/` are generated by `pdf-extract-testkit` from
the recipe catalogue in `crates/testkit/tests/common/corpus/` (our own work,
GPL-3.0-or-later), with the command

    cargo run -p pdf-extract-testkit --example corpus_c

Their manifest entries name the recipe as `testkit::corpus_c::<file>` and are
written by that command, which also records each fixture's compat points,
gate, divergence reason and (hostile files) warning kinds.
`crates/testkit/tests/corpus_c.rs` rebuilds every file and fails unless the
committed bytes and manifest entries are exactly what the recipes produce, so
no per-file rows are needed here. Why each file exists: spec §4.13 and
Appendix C (one or more fixtures per compat point, the open-contract inputs,
and the hostile files small enough to commit).

## Oracle outputs (`expectations/`, `snapshots/`)

`expectations/<sha256>.json` is PyMuPDF 1.28.2's open outcome and page texts
for the fixture with that hash, written by `cd tools/oracle && uv run python
gen.py --prune ../../tests/fixtures/corpus-c ../../tests/fixtures/corpus-b`
(with `--prune`, name every corpus that shares `expectations/`, or its
expectations are deleted), which opens each file from
disk and calls only the public API (L2; see `tools/oracle/README.md`).
`snapshots/<sha256>.txt` is our own output for each `divergence` and
`hostile` fixture,
pinned by `PARITY_BLESS=1 cargo test -p pdf-extract-core --test parity`.
Both are keyed by the fixture's hash, so a regenerated fixture needs both
rerun; `crates/core/tests/parity.rs` (`check_expectations`,
`snapshots_are_referenced`) rejects stale or orphaned files.

## Generated with the oracle (`tools/oracle/mkfixtures.py`)

Files the test kit cannot build because it never encrypts (spec T51). They are
produced by PyMuPDF 1.28.2 used as a black-box tool and committed as
binaries; our own work, under the project's GPL-3.0-or-later license. MuPDF picks a random
file identifier and key on every save, so regenerating changes the bytes and
the hashes (the command rewrites this table and the manifest entries).
Owner password `owner-secret`; the `_user` files also have user password
`user-secret`. Why: spec T6 (owner-only files open transparently; user-password
files fail at open) and the encryption contract rows of §4.8.

## Rasterised by the oracle (corpus D, `tools/oracle/mkcorpusd.py`)

`corpus-d/` is the OCR quality corpus of run 0002 (spec §3.8, Appendix C):
image-only PDFs made by `cd tools/oracle && uv run python mkcorpusd.py`
from the test kit's vector pages (`crates/testkit/src/corpus_d/mod.rs`, our own
work, GPL-3.0-or-later). PyMuPDF 1.28.2 rasterises each page in gray, the
script degrades some with Pillow/numpy, and PyMuPDF re-wraps the pixels as one
image per page. MuPDF randomises the file identifier on save, so the bytes
(not the pixels) change on every run. Each `<name>.txt` beside a PDF is the
ground truth, copied verbatim from the test kit (manifest generator
`testkit::corpus_d::<source>`, so no row here). Why: the §13.4 OCR quality
gate (`crates/ocr/tests/quality.rs`).

every committed binary findable from one place.

## Imported (corpus B)

Sixty text-bearing files from two permissively licensed upstream test suites
(spec §4.14, D-25, Q2), copied byte for byte into `corpus-b/hayro/` and
`corpus-b/pdfbox/`. Gate B (`crates/core/tests/parity.rs`) scores them
against the oracle's expectations; they are test data only and never ship.

- **hayro** — <https://github.com/LaurenzV/hayro>, commit
  `febaff5f79ad7e771971a88f9577736c73f1ca97`, directory
  `hayro-tests/pdfs/custom/`. License: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (the repository's
  `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT`, repeated in `hayro-tests/`).
- **Apache PDFBox** — <https://github.com/apache/pdfbox>, commit
  `c4d556abc9d5f0cbc486d459c84682321dd38ff4`, test resources under the
  paths below. License: Apache-2.0 (the repository's `LICENSE.txt`; its
  appendix puts pre-2008 pdfbox.org contributions under BSD-3-Clause, also
  permissive).

Selection rule (each file was checked, not assumed): the file is committed to
the repository (hayro's `link` entries, downloaded from elsewhere, and
PDFBox's JIRA downloads are not), it was made for that project's own tests
(synthetic, hand-written, or a contributor's own test document), and no
document-level third-party copyright or license notice was found in its text
or metadata (the page text of `sign_me.pdf` reads "Copyright 2014 The Apache
Software Foundation"). Resources embedded in the files do carry their own
notices; they are listed under "Notices inside embedded resources" below.
Skipped as doubtful: real-world documents committed as regression cases
(govdocs and Common Crawl extracts, court filings, journal papers, the CWEB
manual, `test.unc.pdf` with an "Astrium GmbH" notice), files reduced from
users' documents (`*-reduced.pdf`, `pdftc_900k_*`, `lopdf_issue_*`),
the PDF Association's pdf-differences files in hayro (per-file "Copyright
PDF Association" comments), a Stack Overflow sample, and anything password
protected or over ~250 KB. Total size about 1.29 MB.

These files are test inputs only. Neither the wheel nor the sdist contains
them: a release wheel built from this tree holds only `pdf_extract/`, the
compiled extension and the license files, and the sdist holds no PDF at all
(both checked by listing the archives).

### Notices inside embedded resources

Found by searching every decoded stream and object of each file for
copyright, trademark and license strings:

- **Embedded font subsets (programs owned by their foundries):**
  - Calibri, © Microsoft Corporation: `AngledExample`, `PDFA3A`.
  - TimesNewRomanPSMT, © The Monotype Corporation: `FC60_Times`,
    `hello3`, `openoffice-test-document`, `simple-openoffice`.
  - Arial / ArialMT, © The Monotype Corporation: `ControlCharacters`,
    `PDFBOX-4531-bidi-ligature-1`, `unencrypted` (which also embeds
    CourierNewPS-ItalicMT).
  - HelveticaNeue-Medium and -Bold (Apple): `sign_me`.
  - Helvetica and GeezaPro (Apple): `BidiSample`; Helvetica and
    Helvetica-Oblique: `PDFBOX-3110-poems-beads`.
  - Verdana and MSReferenceSansSerif (Microsoft): `sample_fonts_solidconvertor`.
    Their font names have no subset tag, so the programs may be complete
    fonts rather than subsets.
  - Open-licensed fonts (notices kept as embedded): Libertinus Serif
    (OFL-1.1) in hayro's `color_space_lab`, `issue11`,
    `xref_invalid_offsets`; Noto Sans (Google, OFL-1.1) in
    `pattern_shading_on_text`, `pattern_tiling_with_text` and, as Type 3
    glyphs, `font_type3_filled_glyphs`; Liberation Sans/Serif (Red Hat,
    OFL-1.1) in `Annotations`, `with_outline`; Arimo (Apache-2.0) and Noto
    Sans Math (OFL-1.1) in the `GlyphLayout*` files.
- **ICC profiles:** "Copyright (c) 1998 Hewlett-Packard Company" sRGB
  profiles in `BidiSample`, `PDFA3A`, `PDFBOX-3110-poems-beads`,
  `PDFBOX-4531-bidi-ligature-1`, `preEnc_20141025_105451`, `sign_me` and
  `test-landscape2`; `BidiSample` and `PDFBOX-3110-poems-beads` also carry
  an Apple display profile ("Copyright Apple Inc., 2012").
- **Producer strings:** `document.pdf`'s Producer reads "iText® 5.5.0
  ©2000-2013 iText Group NV (AGPL-version)". That names the library that
  wrote the file; the file contains no iText code.

### Per-file notes

- **`corpus-b/hayro/font_type3_filled_glyphs.pdf`** draws three emoji
  (U+1F604, U+1F601, U+1F606) as Type 3 glyphs of a font named
  `TwitterColorEmojiSVGinOT`. They are Twemoji artwork. Twemoji graphics by
  Twitter, Inc and other contributors, licensed under CC-BY 4.0
  (<https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/>); source
  <https://github.com/twitter/twemoji>. The file's producer converted them
  into PDF glyph procedures; we made no further change.
- **`corpus-b/hayro/mask_in_type3_glyph.pdf`** names its Type 3 font
  `SegoeUIEmoji`, but it embeds no font program. Its one glyph is a square
  filled through a luminosity soft mask, with function-based (type 1)
  shadings computed by small PostScript calculator functions (objects 18
  and 20). It holds no
  outline or bitmap data, so only the name refers to Microsoft's Segoe UI
  Emoji.
- **`corpus-b/pdfbox/preEnc_20141025_105451.pdf`** attaches `48.rcpt.pdf`.
  That is a PrivaSphere Secure Messaging receipt produced by a development
  system ("Dev 192.168.1.191", build of 2014-10-24). It contains:
  - the company's address, phone and fax numbers;
  - the role addresses `info@privasphere.com`, `fonoteca@privasphere.com`
    (a test account) and `SecureMessaging@privasphere.com`, which is the
    subject of the Thawte Freemail signing certificate;
  - a Swiss Government TSA timestamp.
  It contains no personal data.
- **`corpus-b/pdfbox/rotation.pdf`** is byte-identical (same SHA-256) to
  pdf.js's `test/pdfs/rotation.pdf`. It was created on 2008-09-15 (Info
  dictionary; author `brianc`, Brian Carrier, a PDFBox committer) and added
  to PDFBox on 2009-02-04 (commit `6434dcc1f7`, PDFBOX-417, path
  `test/input/rotation.pdf`). pdf.js added it on 2011-08-06 (commit
  `4377eed920`). It is therefore attributed to PDFBox, where it originated.
